rows.question: Can I use an AI tool to summarize internal information?
rows.answer: Based on limited supporting evidence, You may use approved AI tools to summarize internal information, provided the data classification allows it. Specifically, approved AI tools may process Public and Internal data. Confidential or Restricted data requires use of an approved tool and a documented business purpose. Additionally, confidential or restricted data must not be pasted into unapproved AI tools. Generated AI output must be reviewed before use in customer communication, policy interpretation, or security decisions.

rows.question: Who should I contact for PTO questions and what is the basic vacation entitlement?
rows.answer: Based on limited supporting evidence, For PTO questions, you should contact People Operations. The basic vacation entitlement for full-time employees is 20 paid vacation days per calendar year, accrued monthly and usable after the first 30 days of employment. Part-time employees receive prorated vacation based on scheduled weekly hours. Employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year, which must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law states otherwise.

Carried-over days must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law requires a different outcome.

rows.question: If I use a personal device for remote work, what are the remote-work and device rules?
rows.answer: Based on limited supporting evidence, If you use a personal device for remote work, you must enroll the device in approved mobile device management or access company resources through approved browser-based tools. Your personal device must have a passcode, a supported operating system, and automatic lock enabled. You are not allowed to download restricted data to personal devices, and confidential data should only be accessed through approved company systems. Additionally, remote work requires using secure networks, avoiding shared public computers, and protecting screens from unauthorized viewing. All remote work must comply with the Device and BYOD Security Policy and the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy.

rows.question: If I work remotely, what approval and device security expectations apply?
rows.answer: If you work remotely, you must first obtain manager approval before changing your regular work location. Temporary changes within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager, while longer changes require People Operations review. Managers consider factors such as team coverage, customer needs, time zone overlap, and data handling requirements before approval. Regarding device security, remote work must comply with the Device and BYOD Security Policy and the Data Classification and Handling Policy. Employees working remotely should use secure networks, avoid shared public computers, and protect screens from unauthorized viewing. Company devices used for remote work must have disk encryption, endpoint protection, automatic screen lock, and current operating system updates, and security tools or device management controls must not be disabled. Personal devices may be used only for limited work access when enrolled in approved mobile device management or accessed through approved browser-based tools, must use a passcode, supported OS, and automatic lock, and must not download restricted data. Confidential data should only be accessed through approved company systems.
